EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Here's How Much a 2025 Rolls-Royce Spectre With 3,000+ Miles Costs in the US
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | mph
Rolls-Royce’s first-ever production electric model, the Spectre , is one of the best luxury grand tourers in its class. Not that there are many left, by the way, yet due to its all-quiet nature, size, and price tag, it does not really have a direct competitor.
It may not show its age yet, though it is already three years old. Deliveries started in the last quarter of 2023, and production takes place at the Goodwood factory in West Sussex, UK. The full-size luxury car could easily transition to an ICE unit, if the company really wanted it, because it is based on the Architecture of Luxury. And this means that it shares numerous nuts and bolts with the Phantom land yacht, the Ghost luxury sedan, and the Cullinan SUV.
Could it eventually gain a gasoline burner? Well, the only one suitable for it would be the hand-built V12, with its twin turbocharged nature, which has a 6.75-liter displacement. And this mill is found on Ghost, Phantom, and Cullinan, in case you forgot. However, while that would be a great addition, this writer believes, it won’t happen, because nothing suggests that Rolls-Royce has something like this in the pipeline for the Spectre .
The model is truly gargantuan for a two-door coupe, as it measures 214.7 inches (5,453 mm) from bumper to bumper. It is 81.9 inches (2,080 mm) wide, 61.4 inches (1,559 mm) tall, and has a wheelbase length of 126.4 inches (3,210 mm). It has a curb weight of almost three metric tons, which is roughly 6,500 pounds, and a future-proof design to die for, both inside and out.
Photo: Instagram | mph If you want to park one of these in your garage, then you must be loaded . That’s because the base model starts from roughly $400,000 in the United States of America for the 2027 model year, whereas the Black Badge variant is around $70,000 more expensive. A nicely-specced example can end up costing you well over half a million dollars, especially if you want the superior Black Badge, which not only gets more goodies, but also offers more oomph.
A used Rolls-Royce Spectre is still on the very expensive side of things, as these tend to fetch from $320,000 to over $500,000 in today’s used car market on our shores, and the value depends on the specification, mileage, and overall condition. Pictured in the gallery is a 2025 model year that features a Black Diamond exterior. It rides on black multi-spoke alloys, has black brake calipers, and is only a few mods away from going down the murdered-out route.
On the inside, this machine features a Muscari Blue look, the vendor reveals. The blue leather upholstery was wrapped around the seats, door cards, center console, and other elements. The lower parts of the dashboard are presented in white, and there is also some black leather upholstery on deck, as well as white piping and stitching. The headliner is black, there are Rolls-Royce emblems embroidered into the headrests, and this thing does not seem to have been visited by the tuning fairy from what we can see.
Photo: Instagram | mph According to the selling dealer, which goes by the name of @mph on Instagram, this particular Rolls-Royce Spectre has a single owner in the papers, and only 3,075 miles (4,949 km) on the clock. Its dual motor setup produces 567 hp (423 kW/575 ps) and 664 pound-feet (900 Nm) of torque. This enables 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in 4.5 seconds. The Black Badge completes the sprint in 4.2 seconds, and has 650 hp (485 kW/659 ps) and 793 lb-ft (1,075 Nm) of torque available via the right pedal.
The vendor mentions a few things about it, including the handcrafted interior, advanced suspension and chassis tech, the magic carpet ride, all-wheel drive, Spirit of Ecstasy hood ornament, and so on, and says that this machine is in stock and ready to be shipped to your doorstep. It appears to be a flawless example, from what we can tell by looking at the pictures shared in the gallery, though for what it’s worth, the driver’s seat appears to show a tiny bit of wear already.
But how much do you think one must fork out if they dream about writing their name on the dotted line of this machine? Well, the pictured Rolls-Royce Spectre, which is a 2025 model year as mentioned above, with just under 3,100 miles under its belt, can be yours today in return for $399,950. And that does not make it affordable, though you may agree to disagree if your bank account has enough digits in it.
Now, if you want to buy this Rolls-Royce Spectre , then you should get in touch with the vendor on social media in order to discuss the details. But would you actually blow $400K on an EV , albeit an extremely luxurious one? View this post on Instagram A post shared by MPH (@mph)
